requirements.requirement: Qualify identity/delegation predicates for issuer, audience, scope, token flows, expiration, key changes and revocation.
Qualify storage/data predicates for schemas, replicas, custody, readers/writers, consistency, retention, residency and inventory reconciliation.
Qualify policy predicates for purpose, consent, authority, access, retention, widening and incompatibility.
Qualify long-running workload predicates for suspension/resume, checkpoints, delayed writes, version coexistence and drainage.
Each installed profile supplies versioned schema, predicates, transitions, diagnostics, fixtures and qualifications without changing kernel meanings.
Distinguish unconditional order, conditional order, coexistence, exclusion, unknown and unsatisfiable constraints.
Analyze strongly connected components and distinguish an invalid order cycle from an explicitly supported coexistence phase.
Expose incompatible plans, unresolved blockers and affected cohorts with requirement-linked explanations.
Generate admissible plans under declared constraints; never treat an optimization ranking as a safety rule.
Reassess planning when declared dependencies, policy or coverage changes; no automatic discovery-completeness inference.
Define allowed lifecycle and side states including blocked, paused, inconclusive, compensating and recovery-required; reject unrestricted reversal.
Derive transition prerequisites from declared profiles, cohort mappings and compatibility constraints.
Retirement requires legacy producer fencing, accepted outstanding-work and stored-state dispositions, consumer readiness and adequate fresh coverage.
Require scoped current authorization and a recovery plan that preserves security floors before retirement.
Dormant/resumable legacy workers block premature retirement; legitimate satisfaction must permit progress.
Targeted rollback affects only authorized cohorts and cannot silently revive revoked authority or discard newer security knowledge.
